argument:
The bull's margin expansion from 32% to 34% alongside 24% revenue growth is clean operating counterevidence after excluding the $98bn investment gain. It answers whether current conversion improved. It does not establish cash available per share after AI investment, financing and dilution, which is the relevant bridge from company operating quality to purchase value.

Senior-note net proceeds of $20.3bn and equity proceeds of $49.6bn still require reconciliation; financing is not automatically evidence of distress, but operating growth alone cannot price its shareholder impact. The 17.38x vendor trailing multiple is distorted by the gain and cannot demonstrate normalised cheapness. Weak-volume recovery adds no reliable tactical edge. I acknowledge substantive operating merit while requiring recurring per-share cash valuation before buying.
key_points: Operating improvement survives the investment-gain objection.
Funding and dilution affect shareholder returns beyond group operating margin.
Gain-distorted trailing P/E cannot establish a bargain.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers current operating conversion well. It explicitly leaves per-share funding and cash returns unresolved, so it does not answer the price objection or justify treating 17.38x as recurring valuation.
